name: make_10_lvl2

input.prompt:
Propose a retrosynthesis route to synthesize the molecule with SMILES CC(F)(F)c1nc(Nc2ccccc2)c2c(OC(/C=C/S(C)(=O)=O)C3CC3)cccc2n1. The route must have 11 reactions.

Here are some guidance to help you (the reactions are enumerated in the order that they must be applied): 1. A Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination couples the aldehyde with diethyl [(methylsulfonyl)methyl]phosphonate. A C=C bond joins the aldehyde carbon to the phosphonate methylene carbon as C-O and C-P bonds are broken, giving the E-alkenyl sulfone.

2. Dess-Martin oxidation converts the primary alcohol to an aldehyde. The C-O single bond becomes C=O without changing the side-chain carbon skeleton.

3. Lithium aluminium hydride reduces the ethyl ester to a primary alcohol. The ester alkoxy C-O bond is cleaved and its carbonyl C=O becomes C-OH, while the quinazoline and aryl ether remain intact.

4. The phenoxide displaces bromide from ethyl 2-bromo-2-cyclopropylacetate. A C-O bond replaces C-Br to install the cyclopropyl-substituted ester side chain as an aryl ether.

5. Hydrolysis of the phenolic acetate cleaves its O-C(=O) bond and regenerates the phenol. The patent combines aniline substitution and deacetylation in one operation; this route represents them as two template applications.

6. Aniline displaces chloride at C4 of the quinazoline by nucleophilic aromatic substitution. A heteroaryl C-N bond replaces C-Cl, producing the N-phenylamino substituent while retaining the acetate protecting group.

7. Thionyl chloride converts the quinazolin-4-one carbonyl to the corresponding 4-chloroquinazoline. The heterocyclic C-O bond is replaced by C-Cl, while the phenolic acetate remains intact.

8. Acetic anhydride protects the phenol as its acetate ester. An O-C(=O) bond forms, replacing the phenolic O-H with an acetyl group before chlorination of the heterocycle.

9. Boron tribromide cleaves the aryl methyl ether to reveal the phenol. The O-CH3 bond breaks while the aryl C-O bond is retained, forming an aromatic hydroxyl group.

10. Cyclocondensation of the anthranilamide with ethyl 2,2-difluoropropionate forms the quinazolin-4-one ring. The ester carbonyl carbon becomes the ring carbon bearing the 1,1-difluoroethyl group. Two C-N bonds form with loss of ethanol and water.

11. Activation of 2-amino-6-methoxybenzoic acid followed by reaction with ammonia converts the carboxylic acid to a primary benzamide. A carbonyl C-N bond replaces the acid C-OH bond; the aromatic amino and methoxy groups are retained.. Note that each of the hint describes the forward reactions for each step (enumerated in the order that they should be applied), but you have to perform the retrosynthetic reactions.
